name: agents-shipgate-triggers
description: Machine-readable trigger catalog for Agents Shipgate. Mirrors the AGENTS.md trigger table — a coding agent can fetch this and apply the rules to a PR diff or repo state to decide whether to run `agents-shipgate verify --preview --json` or the full verifier. Stable for 0.x: rule IDs, predicate vocabulary, and action enum will not change in minor versions.

predicate_vocabulary.glob: Any changed file in the PR matches the glob (relative to repo root). Globstar `**` matches zero or more path segments; `*` matches within a segment; brace expansion is not supported. Matching is case-insensitive, like `boundary_adapter` and the verifier's trust-root classification: Git can carry a spelling (`Policies/`, `agents.md`) that resolves to the canonical governance file on a case-insensitive filesystem, so a case variant must not route differently.
predicate_vocabulary.diff_contains: The unified diff (added or modified lines) of this PR contains the literal string. Use only with stable token forms — decorator names, package names, function calls.
predicate_vocabulary.file_present: The named path exists in the working tree at the head commit, regardless of whether this PR changed it.
predicate_vocabulary.file_absent: The named path does NOT exist in the working tree at the head commit.
predicate_vocabulary.every_file_matches: Every changed file in this PR matches at least one of the listed globs (or the single glob, if a string). False on an empty PR. Matching is case-SENSITIVE, unlike `glob` and `none_match_glob`. This predicate classifies a change set as ignorable, so a wider match produces more skips: case-folding it would read `src/TEST_agent.py` — a legitimate production path on a case-sensitive filesystem — as a test file and skip a PR that adds a tool beside it.
predicate_vocabulary.none_match_glob: No changed file matches any of the listed globs. Same case-insensitive matching as `glob`: it guards a negative rule, so a wider match makes that rule fire less, never more.
predicate_vocabulary.boundary_adapter: Any changed file matches the named entry in `boundary_adapters`. Matching is case-insensitive. The adapter registry is the authoritative path source shared by check, verify, preflight, audit, and triggers.
predicate_vocabulary.none_match_boundary_surface: No changed file matches any path in `boundary_adapters`. Used by negative rules so a host trust root is never treated as a docs-only change.
predicate_vocabulary.any_of: Logical OR over a list of nested predicates.
predicate_vocabulary.all_of: Logical AND over a list of nested predicates.
predicate_vocabulary.detect_returns: Result of `agents-shipgate detect --workspace . --json` matches the given `key: value` pair (`is_agent_project: false`, `suggested_sources: []`, etc.). A key the supplied payload does not carry is *absent*, not false: the block that reads it is then unevaluable rather than satisfied. Used in `stop_conditions` only.
predicate_vocabulary.user_did_not_request: The user did not explicitly ask for a Shipgate run in their prompt. Used in `stop_conditions` only.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes MCP exports, OpenAPI specs, or `tools/*openai*tools*.json`
rules.rationale: MCP exports declare a tool surface; changes need a tool-use readiness check.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes MCP exports, OpenAPI specs, or `tools/*openai*tools*.json`
rules.rationale: OpenAPI specs define HTTP-tool surfaces; scope coverage and side-effect classification depend on them.

rules.rationale: Static tool inventories for the OpenAI and Anthropic Messages APIs are first-class tool sources.

rules.rationale: Repo-local Codex config controls sandboxing, network access, MCP approvals, hooks, and permission profiles; changes need a local boundary check.

rules.rationale: Claude Code project settings and MCP declarations control permissions, hooks, sandboxing, network access, and reachable servers; changes need a local boundary check.

rules.rationale: Cursor project permissions, MCP declarations, and rules define the coding-agent boundary; changes need a local boundary check.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes coding-agent host config, hooks, permissions, MCP servers, or workflows
rules.rationale: VS Code workspace MCP declarations are an experimental host boundary and must fail closed when changed.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes coding-agent host config, hooks, permissions, MCP servers, or workflows
rules.rationale: Workflow permissions, pull_request_target, and write-capable automation are shared coding-agent trust roots.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes Codex plugin manifests, marketplace files, `.app.json`, `.mcp.json`, or `SKILL.md` files
rules.rationale: Codex plugin packages and marketplaces are static release surfaces; plugin metadata, skills, apps, MCP server declarations, and hooks need a readiness check.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes n8n workflow JSON, credential stubs, or n8n tool inventories
rules.rationale: n8n workflow JSON declares an AI tool surface (AI Agent tool sub-nodes, MCP client/server tools, HTTP Request tools); `n8n-nodes-*` node-type tokens are the stable in-diff marker. Changes need a tool-use readiness check.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes Conductor OSS workflow JSON with AI/MCP tasks
rules.rationale: Conductor OSS workflow JSON can declare runtime MCP discovery/calls and LLM tool-selection surfaces; changes need deterministic static review.

rules.agents_md_row: Adds/changes `@function_tool`/`@tool` decorators (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK)
rules.rationale: `@function_tool` / `@tool` (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK) and ADK `FunctionTool(...)` add or modify the tools the agent can call.

A `tools=[...]` argument appears in this diff together with either `LlmAgent(` — a class name no other supported framework uses, so it identifies Google ADK on its own — or a `google.adk` module path alongside an `Agent(` construction. The two legs exist because an edit that adds one tool to an existing agent shows only the constructor and the list; the import sits outside the hunk, so requiring it would miss every modified list and cover only whole-file additions. Plain functions passed to `tools=[...]` carry no decorator, so TRIGGER-FUNCTION-TOOL-DECORATOR never sees them — this rule is what routes an ADK agent's directly reachable tool list. Two forms are deliberately NOT matched. The spaced `tools = [` is TOML array syntax as often as it is Python (it also swallows `enabled_tools = [...]`), and a token that broad is what this catalog is trying to stop reporting as structure. A bare `Agent(` with no ADK token cannot be told apart from CrewAI's `Agent(tools=[...])` by diff text alone, so a *modified* list on the `Agent` alias is out of reach here; closing it needs a signal read from the head file rather than the diff.

Prompts and policy YAML carry approval / confirmation evidence. Trace findings reference these surfaces. The globs match at any depth, and case-insensitively, so a nested or differently-spelled workspace (`services/foo/policies/**`, `enterprise/lib/captain/Prompts/**`) routes exactly like a repo-root one. That is parity with the verifier: `SHIP-VERIFY-TRUST-ROOT-TOUCHED` classifies both surfaces off `TRUST_ROOT_SURFACES`, which has always carried `**/policies/**` and `**/prompts/**`, and the policy check's no-base fail-safe, `SHIP-VERIFY-POLICY-BASE-ABSENT`, additionally treats `**/policies/**` as a fail-safe trust root (its surface list covers the manifest, policies and `.agents-shipgate/`, not prompts). A root-only, case-sensitive trigger reported edits those checks call governance-bearing as `no_match`. The `**/`-prefixed and bare forms are both listed because a consumer applying this catalog with a glob engine where `**/` requires at least one leading segment would otherwise lose the repo-root match.

The manifest is the source of truth for the release gate. The glob matches at any depth: a monorepo keeps one manifest per project directory (`services/refund/shipgate.yaml`), and a root-only rule reported an edit to the very file that declares a project's agent, purpose, and tool surface as `no_match`. The `**/`-prefixed and bare forms are both listed for the same reason as the prompts/policies rule: a consumer whose glob engine requires a leading segment for `**/` would otherwise lose the repo-root match.
CI gate changes touch the release-readiness path itself.

rules.agents_md_row: Repo already opted in (shipgate.yaml present in the workspace)
rules.rationale: Repo already opted in; run on every PR — including docs-only — because the manifest's existence is the operational opt-in. `force_run` overrides any `skip_shipgate` rule that would otherwise fire (e.g. a docs-only PR in an opted-in repo).

rules.agents_md_row: (Optional) Refactor or framework upgrade that may shift the extracted tool surface
rules.rationale: Two signals co-occur: a supported-framework package token appears somewhere in this diff, AND a dependency manifest is among the changed files. That co-occurrence is the whole of the evidence — the rule does not confirm that any version moved, and a bare token in prose or sample code no longer matches on its own. A framework upgrade can shift the statically extracted tool surface, so an advisory dry-run is a no-cost defensive check. (The rule ID is retained for 0.x compatibility; read this rationale, not the ID, for what was observed.)

rules.agents_md_row: Pure read-only doc/test changes with no manifest impact
rules.rationale: Docs-only OR tests-only PR; no tool surface impact. Covers the AGENTS.md row 'Pure read-only doc/test changes' — a tests/ directory edit that incidentally mentions `@tool` in a fixture or assertion no longer falsely triggers Shipgate.

stop_conditions.description: Stop and do not propose Shipgate when ALL of these hold (mirrors AGENTS.md "Stop conditions" prose). Every negative in this conjunction is a claim about the whole workspace, which is why `agent_scope_truncated: false` belongs in it: a detect run whose Python parse stopped at its cap read only part of the repository, and `is_agent_project: false` from a partial read is not a reason to stop. A `detect` payload that does not carry every key named here leaves the block unevaluable — `stop_conditions_evaluated` is false and no stop is inferred.

actions.force_run: Propose Shipgate unconditionally. Overrides `skip_shipgate` rules — used when the repo has explicitly opted in (e.g. existing `shipgate.yaml`) and every PR should be checked.
actions.run_shipgate: Propose `agents-shipgate verify --preview --json` as the next step; if preview says the repo needs configuration, use supporting setup commands before the full verifier. Does NOT win over `skip_shipgate` — a docs-only PR that incidentally mentions a tool decorator stays skipped.
actions.skip_shipgate: Do not propose Shipgate. Beats `run_shipgate` (but loses to `force_run`). Recommend other appropriate checks for the PR.
actions.dry_run: Advisory: `run_shipgate` stays false but `dry_run_recommended` is true in the evaluator output. Callers may propose a non-mutating scan; never propose `init --write` based on `dry_run` alone.
